t:
(a) General Rule.—If a qualified airline employee receives any airline payment amount and transfers any portion of such amount to a Roth IRA within 180 days of receipt of such amount (or, if later, within 180 days of the date of the enactment of this Act), then such amount (to the extent so transferred) shall be treated as a qualified rollover contribution described in section 408A(e) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, and the limitations described in section 408A(c)(3) of such Code shall not apply to any such transfer. 
    (b) Definitions and Special Rules.—For purposes of this section—
        (1) Airline payment amount.—
            (A) In general.—The term “airline payment amount” means any payment of any money or other property which is payable by a commercial passenger airline carrier to a qualified airline employee—
                (i) under the approval of an order of a Federal bankruptcy court in a case filed after September 11, 2001, and before January 1, 2007, and 
                (ii) in respect of the qualified airline employee’s interest in a bankruptcy claim against the carrier, any note of the carrier (or amount paid in lieu of a note being issued), or any other fixed obligation of the carrier to pay a lump sum amount.   The amount of such payment shall be determined without regard to any requirement to deduct and withhold tax from such payment under sections 3102(a) and 3402(a).
            (B) Exception.—An airline payment amount shall not include any amount payable on the basis of the carrier’s future earnings or profits.  
        (2) Qualified airline employee.—The term “qualified airline employee” means an employee or former employee of a commercial passenger airline carrier who was a participant in a defined benefit plan maintained by the carrier which—
            (A) is a plan described in section 401(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 which includes a trust exempt from tax under section 501(a) of such Code, and 
            (B) was terminated or became subject to the restrictions contained in paragraphs (2) and (3) of section 402(b) of the Pension Protection Act of 2006.  
        (3) Reporting requirements.—If a commercial passenger airline carrier pays 1 or more airline payment amounts, the carrier shall, within 90 days of such payment (or, if later, within 90 days of the date of the enactment of this Act), report—
            (A) to the Secretary of the Treasury, the names of the qualified airline employees to whom such amounts were paid, and 
            (B) to the Secretary and to such employees, the years and the amounts of the payments.   Such reports shall be in such form, and contain such additional information, as the Secretary may prescribe. 
    (c) Effective Date.—This section shall apply to transfers made after the date of the enactment of this Act with respect to airline payment amounts paid before, on, or after such date.

fable.w: The section sets tax rollover treatment for airline bankruptcy payments and requires carriers to report payment information to the Treasury Secretary and employees. The tempting reading is that carriers reporting to the Secretary, or the Secretary's power to "prescribe" the form of reports, amounts to outside involvement or rulemaking. But the reporting is a compliance duty rather than consultation on a federal decision, and prescribing a report's form is not an explicit rulemaking, comment, hearing, advisory or right-to-sue process.
fable.s: Such reports shall be in such form, and contain such additional information, as the Secretary may prescribe.

qwen_block.w: This section describes a mechanism for airline employees to transfer bankruptcy payments into Roth IRAs and imposes reporting requirements on the airlines. The reporting is directed to the Secretary of the Treasury (inside the government) and the employees themselves. There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with outside parties, hold public hearings, or coordinate with states/tribes before making a decision. The interaction described is administrative reporting and individual benefit processing, not participatory decision-making.
qwen_block.s: If a commercial passenger airline carrier pays 1 or more airline payment amounts, the carrier shall, within 90 days of such payment (or, if later, within 90 days of the date of the enactment of this Act), report— (A) to the Secretary of the Treasury, the names of the qualified airline employees to whom such amounts were paid, and (B) to the Secretary and to such employees, the years and the amounts of the payments.

opus.w: This section treats certain airline bankruptcy payments as qualified Roth IRA rollovers and requires carriers to report payment details to Treasury. Those reports are routine compliance filings, not consultation or comment on a federal decision. Letting the Secretary set the report format is a ministerial detail, not a clear grant of authority to make rules. The word 'participant' refers only to people in a pension plan. No outside party gets a role in shaping a federal decision.
opus.s: Such reports shall be in such form, and contain such additional information, as the Secretary may prescribe.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting readings:** Airlines must report to the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Secretary may set the form of those reports. That could look like an outsider talking to an agency, or like authority to write rules (Example 6). Neither holds up. The airlines are sending required information on payments already made. They are not giving input on a federal decision. The phrase "as the Secretary may prescribe" only covers the format of a compliance report. It does not grant authority to issue regulations. The word "participant" in "participant in a defined benefit plan" is only a keyword match. The bankruptcy court order is part of a definition and does not involve outsiders in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines tax treatment for airline payments and requires airlines to report payment details to the Secretary of the Treasury. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits and mere reporting/notification obligations from the scope of participation. The interaction described is a compliance requirement for data submission, not a consultation, advisory role, or public comment period influencing a federal decision.
qwen_chat.s: (3) Reporting requirements.—If a commercial passenger airline carrier pays 1 or more airline payment amounts, the carrier shall, within 90 days of such payment (or, if later, within 90 days of the date of the enactment of this Act), report— (A) to the Secretary of the Treasury, the names of the qualified airline employees to whom such amounts were paid, and (B) to the Secretary and to such employees, the years and the amounts of the payments.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the reporting requirements in subsection (b)(3) constitute participation because they involve interaction between the airline (an outside entity) and the Secretary of the Treasury. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses" and mere reporting/notification obligations are not participation. Reporting data to the government is an administrative compliance requirement, not a process where the outside party consults with or influences a federal decision-making process. The section deals with tax treatment of payments and reporting those payments, which falls under the "No" category for applications/reporting.
